argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than a clean compliance finding. The admissible record supports certification only on a constrained basis: the current release shows an aggregate readiness pass and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while policy and public governance guidance allow deployment decisions to rest on current measurement, documentation, monitoring, and explicit limitation disclosure. The same admissible record also shows a live debt-collection segment weakness below threshold, and it does not show approved mitigation or risk acceptance. That means prior approval and informal monitoring can only be treated as context. The audit concern is valid if it reads the packet as claiming present full compliance; it is overstated if it ignores that the packet can still support a caveated certification theory grounded in aggregate readiness plus required disclosure of the current segment limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is offered as a basis for the determination. The requested treatment is based on policy-permitted narrowing of the certification theory, not on schedule pressure or launch cost.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit stale approval or informal monitoring to substitute for current evidence. But policy also does not require the segment weakness to be fully resolved if the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material weakness is disclosed, absent approved mitigation. On the admissible evidence, the defendable policy position is therefore not clean compliance; it is that certification is supportable only as caveated compliance tied expressly to current documentation of the debt-collection weakness.
concessions: The current record does not establish that the required disclosure is already present in the release documentation.
The debt-collection compliance slice is a material current weakness for the named use case.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot carry this release.
The manual-monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or disclosure language.
